newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela first half joblessness rises to 12.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela first half joblessness rises to 12.4 pct.

text.p: Venezuelan unemployment rose to 12.4 percent of the workforce in the second half of 1996, or 1,122,119 people, up from 10.2 percent in the second half of 1995, according to the Central Statistical Office (OCEI).

The OCEI defines unemployment as the percentage of the workforce, aged 15 or over, currently without paid work but actively searching for employment. Just over nine million workers made up the Venezuelan workforce in the second half of 1996, the OCEI said.

The OCEI said construction showed the highest sectoral level of unemployment, at 20.5 percent or 154,000 people during the second half of 1996, compared to 20.4 percent over the first half of 1996 and 16.9 percent in the second half of 1995.

According to the OCEI's half yearly household survey, the number of workers employed in Venezuela's informal sector also grew to 48.7 percent, or 3,849,000 people, from 48.4 percent during the same period in 1995.
The informal sector is defined as those working in domestic service, self-employed non-professionals and those employed in businesses with less than five people.
